title: Please make Maxmind's geoipupdate an optional dependency (or call the command externally)
body:
### What happened?

While updating the Debian package to the latest release I noticed this new dependency: Maxmind's geoipupdate.  Unfortunately we can't use this in Debian because it's a non-free service (https://<redacted-host>/) that costs money.

Would you please make this dependency optional, or better yet call the geoipupdate executable as an external command?

Making it optional will mean that all Debian users (including educational, commercial, scientific, etc) lose access to the feature--even subscribers to the paid service.  Making it possible to call the executable will mean that anyone can opt-in simply by installing the non-free software.

I hope this sounds reasonable to you :)
Thanks again for this wonderful software!

P.S. My team member @participant3 suggested the opt-in approach, which looks like the ideal solution to us

### Syncthing version

v1.27.9

### Platform & operating system

Debian

### Browser version

NA

### Relevant log output

```shell
NA
```

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: P.S. Sorry I forgot to mention this is a blocking issue to updating the package in Debian to--or beyond--the Syncthing version where the dependency was introduced.  There's no urgent need, since we need to wait for a new dependency to be accepted before uploading 1.27.7, but it would be nice to see in 1.27.10.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> [...] Unfortunately we can't use this in Debian because it's a non-free service (https://<redacted-host>/) that costs money. [...]
>
> Making it optional will mean that all Debian users (including educational, commercial, scientific, etc) lose access to the feature--even subscribers to the paid service. [...]

Can you expand on that please? The new dependency is client code dual licensed MIT and Apache 2, both are compatible with DFSG. I am not aware that interacting with non-free services makes a software non-free in debian. Especially the part about costing money/paid service confuses me - debian isn't about free as in beer, something can absolutely be compatible with DFSG and carry a price (not claiming maxmind's offering is that - we aren't packaging/shipping it).

I can see that it would be nicer if one could use other services or none at all for this functionality, but that seems like a reasonable feature request not a problem for debian packaging. And as participant1 said, barrying examples of actual users of the relay pool, a pretty low importance one.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Simon Frei ***@***.***> writes:

>> [...] Unfortunately we can't use this in Debian because it's a non-free service (https://<redacted-host>/) that costs money. [...]
>>
>> Making it optional will mean that all Debian users (including educational, commercial, scientific, etc) lose access to the feature--even subscribers to the paid service. [...]
>
> Can you expand on that please? The new dependency is client code dual licensed MIT and Apache 2, both are compatible with DFSG. I am not aware that interacting with non-free services makes a software non-free in debian. Especially the part about costing money/paid service confuses me - debian isn't about free as in beer, something can absolutely be compatible with DFSG and carry a price (not claiming maxmind's offering is that - we aren't packaging/shipping it).

I'm happy to expand on this this time.

First, the part that isn't my call: Maxmind's geoipupdate has been part
of the "contrib" section of the archive for some time, and this section
is not part of Debian.
  https://www.debian.org/doc/debian-policy/ch-archive.html#the-contrib-archive-area

"Contrib" is for legalistically free-software that is useless without
non-free things (mandatory subscriptions, proprietary firmware or
databases, trade secrets, toxic candy, non-free EULAs etc).  My
understanding is that Maxmind's geoipupdate was relegated to "contrib"
because it is useless without a signing up for an account to gain access
to a nonredistributable and problematic proprietary database.

  https://maxmind.com
  https://<redacted-host>/geoip/geolite2-free-geolocation-data
    * Not free because of "Discrimination Against Fields of
      Endeavors" https://www.debian.org/social_contract.1.0
                 https://<redacted-host>/en/geolite2/eula
    * Various other restrictions in the EULA (ie §10, the bait and
      switch clause for a notice many users would not ever see)
    * §6.c !  It should be clear to anyone who takes the time to read
      the EULA that this sort of thing has no place in FLOSS.
    * "for any conflicts among the above 4 documents, the priority and
      precedence of interpretation is DPA, PP, WT and Creative Commons
      License."  This is a huge red flag that means "call your lawyers,
      here be dragons"...which is the literal meaning of draconian.

Software in "main" cannot link with, Depend on, Build-Depend on, or
Recommend software in "contrib" or in "non-free"; however, software in
"main" can Suggest (ie: user-initiated opt-in run-time plugins, call
optional external executables, etc) software in contrib or in non-free.

> I can see that it would be nicer if one could use other services or none at all, but that seems like a reasonable feature request not a problem for debian packaging. And as participant1 said, barrying examples of actual users of the relay pool, a pretty low importance one.
>

Please see my previous message; this is a hard-blocking issue.  Without
a fix, users of our package are stuck with 1.27.7 or maybe
1.27.8--I haven't investigated 1.27.8 yet.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Right, so, to summarise:

- Debian doesn't like the maxmind package for whatever reason
- Syncthing (the user facing program) doesn't have that package as a dependency
- The two programs that currently do have that as a dependency are `cmd/strelaypoolsrv` (the relay pool server) and `cmd/ursrv` (the usage reporting server), neither of which should be distributed by Debian imho, since they have almost zero utility for anyone but ourselves

Building syncthing as we recommend (`go run build.go build syncthing`) doesn't build or require the maxmind package. Syncthing doesn't have any kind of geo-ip functionality. So, for this issue, it is not only an optional dependency, it's not a dependency at all for the things that should be distributed.

If Debian are building things in some other manner I suggest adjusting that. Anything that in the end results in something like `go build ./cmd/syncthing` should be fine.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Simon Frei ***@***.***> writes:

> Yeah thanks for explaining the contrib vs non-free distinction, should have expressed that explicitly before.
>
> And we have progress: Originally it was about patching out the maxmind
> library, now it's not using relay pool srv.

No, that was a preemptive compromise I was offering to make things
easier for you.

> That's already possible: `go run build.go build <target>`, where target corresponds to a binary/package name in `./cmd`.

This is from a developer perspective :)  It's not possible to do this
from a Debian packaging perspective.  You used to have a build system
that would iterate over targets, create a list, then build the list.  At
that time we used the following to skip unwanted (or prohibited
targets):

  export DH_GOLANG_EXCLUDES := cmd/strelaypoolsrv \
                             cmd/stcli \
                             cmd/stcrashreceiver \
                             cmd/stupgrades \
                             meta($$|/) \
                             cmd/ursrv
  https://salsa.debian.org/go-team/packages/syncthing/-/blob/master/debian/rules?ref_type=heads#L28

I'm not sure where in the Go ecosystem this broke, but Syncthing wasn't
the only one that lost support, even though most packages still fully
support it.

They're not distributed in Debian, but for some reason your
configuration enforces them.  Please see the message I just sent.

I'm sorry but this isn't possible within a Debian packaging context.
Please see my willingness to save you effort and time even if that means
compromising.  It's still the Golang team's position that it would be
best to make it possible to build strelaypoolsrv without maxmind (or
using an alternative geoipupdate implementation).

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I'm not seeing much sense made here, sorry. However you do your build, building Syncthing *does not require* the maxmind/geoupdate package. It doesn't need to be present on disk, it doesn't get downloaded, it doesn't get parsed.

Even assuming we still somehow thought it was a problem that it's mentioned in the module requirements, I'm not sure what you're even asking. What is an "optional dependency" that you want us to make it, when it's already *not* a dependency?

If Debians build system is unable to build a normal Go program in the normal way, can it run a pre-script? If so, add this:

```
rm -rf cmd/strelaypoolsrv cmd/ursrv lib/geoip
go mod tidy
```

and the affected pieces of code are gone.

comments.body:
> > It's still the Golang team's position that it would be

@participant3 Wow, way to throw a team member under the bus...  I opened this issue because you asked me to, advocated for your approach, and I would not have opened this issue nor CCed you in the initial message were this not the case.

Yes, it also appears something upstream broke our clean `DH_GOLANG_EXCLUDES` opt-out approach, and I've heard Syncthing isn't the only affected package, so it's not worth wasting any more Syncthing devs time on this issue.

@participant1 @participant2 thank you for taking the time to engage with this issue--I truly appreciate it.  For this issue to have not been a waste of time, please note that Maxmind expects all GeoLite2 users to keep records that prove that they always have the most up-to-date copy of the GeoIP database.  By using the Geolite2 you also agree to send them hardcopy papermail proof of compliance should they ever request it.  This is in their EULA.  For the record, I'm not a lawyer and this is not legal advice.  That said, I hope that this you can profit from discovery by preparing in advance :)
